judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the site-search text field in the collapsed Business mega-menu (input #global-header--search-track-business), inside a form with role="search" that submits to usps.com/search, with a visually hidden label "Search USPS.com" and the placeholder "Search or Enter a Tracking Number". The snapshot and the live page (unchanged as of 2026-10-11) confirm this. 2.4.6 asks that a label describe the control's topic or purpose. "Search USPS.com" does that: it is a search box for this site, and what you type into a search box is a search term. Accepting tracking numbers as well is an extra feature that the placeholder mentions. WCAG does not require a label to list every kind of input it accepts. Asking for the label to say "what to enter" in full is stricter than 2.4.6.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The element is the header site-search field revealed by the Search (magnifier) menu item (input #global-header--search-track-search), inside a form with role="search" and a submit button, with a visually hidden label "Search USPS.com" and the placeholder "Search or Enter a Tracking Number". It matches the live page as of 2026-10-11. The label describes the purpose of the field, searching USPS.com, which is all 2.4.6 asks of a label. The search being able to take a tracking number does not make "Search USPS.com" non-descriptive. Calling the label a failure because it does not name every accepted input applies a stricter rule than WCAG 2.4.6.
